[oig.justice.gov](https://oig.justice.gov/sites/default/files/archive/special/s0606/chapter4.htm?utm_source=chatgpt.com) |

primary_source_passages_reused.text: Around 9:30 a.m. on the same morning, Dwight began drafting in the CIA’s computer system a CIR addressed to the UBL Unit Chief at FBI Headquarters and an SSA in the UBL Unit at FBI Headquarters who we call “Bob.” Dwight’s CIR also was addressed to the FBI’s New York Field Office. The CIR first described the NSA information that had been received about Mihdhar, including the planned travel to Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia in early January. The CIR also discussed the potential links between the suspected terrorist facility in the Middle East and the 1998 East Africa embassy bombings. The CIR stated that photographs of Mihdhar had been obtained and would be sent to the FBI under separate cover. The CIR detailed Mihdhar’s passport and visa information, including that Mihdhar had listed on his visa application his intended destination as New York and that he planned to stay three months. Dwight also wrote that the CTC was requesting “feedback” on “any intelligence uncovered in FBI’s investigation” resulting from the information in the CIR.

primary_source_passages_reused.text: To investigate the issues involving Hazmi and Mihdhar, the OIG asked for and reviewed all documents the FBI had regarding them before September 11. The FBI search for these documents included searches of its Automated Case Support system (ACS), Integrated Intelligence Information Application (IIIA) system, 94 and CTLink. 95 In addition, searches were conducted on archived FBI e-mail messages and the FBI Director’s briefing documents. These searches were initially conducted in response to a request by the Congressional Joint Intelligence Committee’s Inquiry Staff, which was conducting its own inquiry into this subject. The OIG also obtained direct access to ACS so that we could conduct our own searches for relevant documents. In addition, we reviewed hard copy case and informant files to search for documents relevant to Mihdhar and Hazmi.

primary_source_passages_reused.text: In February 2004, however, while we were reviewing a list of CIA documents that had been accessed by FBI employees assigned to the CIA, we noticed the title of a document that appeared to be relevant to this review and had not been previously disclosed to us. 2. FBI informant handling and payment.

original_assessment_wording.exact_original_wording: | **The FBI-informant landlord proves government direction** | **A real and troubling relationship; direction is not established.** Hazmi and Mihdhar lived with an FBI asset. That supports serious scrutiny, not a demonstrated conclusion that the FBI controlled the hijackers. supporting_passages.text: OIG note 133 reports that the initially unpaid asset received $100,000 and was closed as an asset in July 2003.

contrary_passages.text: The asset and retired handler were not interviewed directly by OIG, although the handler had spoken to FBI supervisors and congressional investigators. OIG notes an inconclusive polygraph and the San Diego FBI conclusion that the asset was not complicit. None should be dropped.

The lack of a specific boarder rule and disagreement among other agents are contrary to a blanket “proved rule violation” characterization. The policy review still identifies a concrete oversight weakness.
The note does not establish what the payment compensated, who approved it or why the asset was closed. A hush-payment or protection theory is a hypothesis, not a result of reading the amount.

primary_source_passages_reused.text: The OIG was not able to interview the asset. The Joint Intelligence Committee Inquiry had attempted to interview the asset without success. tasks.exact_original_request_wording:
8. Audit our own evaluation across every track.
- Verify the exact film edition and timestamp behind each attributed documentary claim.
- Recheck “supported,” “false,” and “unsubstantiated” labels against the actual source and its limitations.
- Count independent evidentiary chains, not repeated reports, aliases, hosts, table rows, or calls automatically treated as separate conversations.
- Distinguish records we have not obtained from records demonstrably withheld, lost, or destroyed.
- Scrutinize dismissals and suspicions equally. Record negative results, alternative hypotheses, and what evidence would change each conclusion.
- Keep assistance, foreknowledge, deliberate nonintervention, demolition, and later concealment separate. Connected circumstantial evidence can matter without a confession; its independence and connections still require demonstration.

original_assessment_wording.exact_original_wording: **My overall assessment is that the two films have substantially different evidentiary records.**

**A plausible innocent explanation does not erase an observation’s evidentiary weight.** Nor must a case produce a confession or explicit written order: sufficiently connected circumstantial evidence can establish coordination.

The useful cumulative question is whether these findings converge on **the same actors, communications, money flows, access, or objectives**. They already establish important things individually: deliberate destruction, blocked dissemination, concrete assistance, and impaired scrutiny. Their significance should not be reduced to “nothing proves the entire hypothesis.”

At the same time, **concealing interrogation abuse, protecting institutional reputations, limiting liability, and concealing participation in an attack are different purposes**. Establishing concealment does not automatically identify which purpose explains it.
